summary: 10 concrete recommendations surfaced from 30 fully crawled HN front-page stories.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Meshdiff
items.source_story_title: Meshdiff – visually compare two STL versions in the browser, client-side
items.summary: A local-first browser tool for visually comparing two STL versions.
items.why_included: A commenter specifically praised its local-first design and roadmap.
items.evidence: A commenter called it very cool work and highlighted its client/local-first emphasis.

evidence_sources.author: sota_pop
evidence_sources.excerpt: Very cool work! Nice job. Road-map looks good too! I always appreciate client/local-first emphasis.

items.name: F*
items.source_story_title: F*: A general-purpose proof-oriented programming language
items.summary: A proof-oriented programming language for verified systems and incremental C migration.
items.why_included: A practitioner reported a solid experience using it around existing C code.
items.evidence: One commenter liked F*'s external-library support while incrementally migrating C codebases and called it very solid.

evidence_sources.author: pvsnp
evidence_sources.excerpt: I liked being able to express calling external libraries while incrementally migrating existing C codebases to F*. Very solid language.

items.name: Bor
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Bor – Open-source policy management for Linux desktops
items.summary: An open-source system for centrally managing Linux desktop policies.
items.why_included: It addresses a concrete Linux fleet-management gap for a commenter managing nonprofit laptops.
items.evidence: A laptop administrator said Bor was close to what they needed and wanted to try it.

evidence_sources.author: V__
evidence_sources.excerpt: This looks really close to what I need. I manage a few laptops for a non-profit.

items.name: Kakehashi
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Kakehashi – Experimental userspace to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM
items.summary: An experimental Linux ARM userspace for running macOS binaries.
items.why_included: The project drew clear demand for its longer-term Mac application compatibility goal.
items.evidence: A commenter said they had waited a long time for this direction and would follow its progress closely.

evidence_sources.author: leothetechguy
evidence_sources.excerpt: this is something I've been waiting for a long time. I will be watching this with great interest.

items.name: NixOS-DGX-Spark
items.source_story_title: Show HN: NixOS-DGX-Spark – Nix and NixOS on the DGX Spark
items.summary: Nix and NixOS configuration for NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware.
items.why_included: A practitioner reported a successful deployment across several related Asus machines.
items.evidence: A commenter said they had been running it on several Asus GX10 machines with k3s and found it great.

evidence_sources.author: redrove
evidence_sources.excerpt: Been running this on a few Asus GX10 machines with k3s on top, it’s been great.

items.name: Flexify 2
items.summary: A Photoshop plugin for transforming images into unusual map projections.
items.why_included: A long-time user called it incredible and used it for a school paper-globe project.
items.evidence: A commenter described Flexify as incredible and recalled using it with NASA maps to make polyhedral paper planets.

evidence_sources.author: rgovostes
evidence_sources.excerpt: is an incredible decades-old Photoshop plugin for making these.

items.name: pydymax
items.summary: A Python library for turning 360-degree photographs into isospheres.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it as a free terminal-based route for this workflow.
items.evidence: A commenter said they had used pydymax to make isospheres from 360 photographs.

evidence_sources.author: blululu
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have used this python libraries to make isospheres from 360 photographs: https://github.com/Teque5/pydymax

items.name: FastTracker II Clone
items.source_story_title: Fasttracker II clone in C using SDL 2
items.summary: A modern C and SDL 2 clone of the classic FastTracker II music tracker.
items.why_included: A former user said the original started a lifelong fascination with electronic music making.
items.evidence: A commenter praised the resurrection of FastTracker II after describing how it opened up electronic music creation for them.

evidence_sources.author: tomduncalf
evidence_sources.excerpt: So thank you to the author for resurrecting this amazing and somewhat esoteric bit of software!

items.name: Holocloth
items.summary: An interactive holographic cloth-effect web experiment.
items.why_included: It received unambiguous aesthetic praise as a lightweight creative experiment.
items.evidence: A commenter said they loved holographic effects and found Holocloth gorgeous.

evidence_sources.author: ghosty141
evidence_sources.excerpt: I don't know why but I just LOVE holographic effects. Looks gorgeous!

items.name: Phanteks T30-120
items.source_story_title: ASRock BC-250: Building the Budget Steam Machine
items.summary: A 120 mm PC fan recommended for high-airflow custom cooling builds.
items.why_included: A detailed comparison presented it as a substantially higher-airflow option with a better noise character.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended fitting the Phanteks T30-120 for 105 CFM and described its noise as pleasant white noise.

evidence_sources.author: altairprime
evidence_sources.excerpt: then you can fit the Phanteks T30-120 which hits 105CFM at 43.6dBa, beating the P12 by a solid +30CFM for +4dBa.
